Part 1

What does the outside operator see that the board cannot, and how is each item identified?

Part 1 · the plan

From the board to the plant itself

  1. What the board missesgauges, hand valves, seals, stems
  2. The unit at true scalethirteen items on one plot plan
  3. Colours and tagshow a line and a gauge are identified
  4. The 3-D viewtour labels and identify mode

Why go outside

The board sees transmitters; the round sees the plant

Alarms tell you something changed; the round finds what.

On the board

Transmitter values, controller outputs, alarms and trips.

Only in the field

  • 19 hand valves: position seen by eye
  • Car seals and locks on four of them
  • Stems of 14 control, trip and relief valves
  • 43 field gauges read where they stand

Leaks, frost, noise, vibration: real round items, not modelled in this OTS.

The colour names the fluid

Colours follow the board’s convention — the colour tells the fluid before the line number does.

Interactive — pick a first letter

The first letter names the measurement

The number places the item in its loop — read the letters before the number.

Same stop, two label modes

Tour shows the answer; Identify asks for it

Station 5: feed battery limit and E-101, from the OTS page.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Hand valves, seals, locks and stems are seen only in the field.
  • The 3-D unit is the Layout tab’s plot plan at true size.
  • Colour gives the fluid; the tag letters give the measurement.
  • Tour labels teach; Identify mode tests.

The rounds sheet’s rule

A reading passes inside a band set by the span

$\delta$
pass band either side of the plant value
gauge unit
$r_{lo}, r_{hi}$
transmitter range ends
gauge unit
$d$
decimals shown on the gauge
–
$$\delta = \max\!\left(0.02\,(r_{hi}-r_{lo}),\; 2\times10^{-d}\right)$$
$\delta_{PI\text{-}206} = \max(0.02 \times 25,\; 0.02) = 0.5$ barrange 0–25 bar a, two decimals
$\delta_{AI\text{-}114} = \max(0.02 \times 10,\; 0.02) = 0.2$ mol%range 0–10 mol%

Valve openings pass within ±5 %; states by their first word.

Interactive — station, row, then your reading

The 28 rows of the rounds sheet

From the last slide$\delta = \max\left(0.02\,(r_{hi}-r_{lo}),\, 2\times10^{-d}\right)$

The band follows the transmitter span — a wide-range gauge forgives more than a narrow one.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Twelve stations, about 410 m, control room to control room.
  • Every gauge and hand valve has one stop on the route.
  • 18 gauges at grade, 15 on decks, 10 on platforms.
  • A reading passes within 2 % of the transmitter span.

Part 3

What do the hand valves do, and how do field, board and model compare?

Part 3 · the plan

From a valve’s position to the plant’s response

  1. Four classes of hand valveopen, closed, car-sealed, locked
  2. Each valve and its jobwhat happens out of position
  3. A valve out of position, on the modelthree replays
  4. Field, board, model, logwhat is the same, what is added
  5. The field exercisesas the trainee sees them

19 hand valves of the rev B P&ID, tagged on the Layout tab

Each class behaves differently on the round

The round found them; now, what are they for?

NO · 11

Block valves: open. Operable.

NC · 4

Bypass globes: closed. Operable.

LO · 1

MV-314 under PSV-314. Refuses to close.

LC · 3

Drains. Permit to unlock first.

Handwheel green open, red closed; yellow tag on a seal or lock.

Interactive — click a hand valve

Normal position, and what the plant does if it is wrong

No hand-valve position reaches the board — a valve left wrong shows up only as a process upset.

Interactive — model run from design, no operator action

Seconds or minutes: it depends on the valve

MV-202 trips K-201 in 5 s; MV-103 trips K-301 after 3.5 min — the slower the upset, the more a round can catch.

How the tab is built

Same numbers outside; one addition to the model

The replays used the same model the gauges show.

Field gauge

Shows the board’s own measurement of the model, noise included.

Hand valves

Model addition. All at normal: design unchanged, largest drift 0.003 in 10 min.

Not modelled

Labels show through steel; no collisions; fixed eye levels.

Interactive — pick a field action

Every action leaves one line in the log

Exercises tick themselves from these lines — an action that leaves no line did not happen.

Interactive — as the trainee sees them

Eight field exercises and a check in every training case

The situations say what to do, never why — the round itself is the exercise.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • 19 hand valves: 11 NO, 4 NC, 1 LO, 3 LC.
  • Out of position, a valve trips a machine in seconds or starves a kettle in minutes.
  • Field gauges read the board’s numbers; hand valves leave design unchanged.
  • Every field action is logged and graded.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Walk all twelve stations; the board cannot show a hand valve.

2

Identify each line by colour and each gauge by its letters first.

3

Record readings within 2 % of span and compare them with the board.

4

Check every hand valve against its normal position; never close a car-sealed one.
